title: Weeknote: OKR scratchpad & micro-metrics
content:
Purpose:
- Quick self-check each Friday to calibrate work vs. OKRs & keep micro-metrics visible.
- Lightweight: capture evidence, decisions, blockers, and 1-3 actions for next week.

OKR draft (Q1-Q2 stretch):
- Objective: Reduce median host API inference latency while keeping token cost within +/-5% of baseline.
  - KR1: Median token latency (100 seq) down from 85ms -> 60ms for hosted small/med models (measure: median p95 across region).
  - KR2: Per-token cost decrease by 8% on average across top 5 endpoints (batching + cache improvements).
  - KR3: Two infra rollouts completed with no >1% error-rate regression (canary + auto-fallback).

This week (2026-03-04 -> 2026-03-10) quick log:
- Focus: prefix cache prototype + small-model kernel swap A/B.
- Wins:
  - Cache prototype reduced repeated-prefix token emit by ~22% in synthetic bench (local harness). Evidence: bench-run-0310.csv (see linked PR).
  - Kernel swap for small-med model passed perf smoke tests; p50 improved ~10ms.
- Signals/metrics observed:
  - Synthetic bench: median end-to-end per-token latency 68ms (target 60ms).
  - Prod-like staging: cold-start variance still large on <8seq cases (p95 spikes).

Blockers / open questions:
- Autoscaler config interaction: caching introduces uneven CPU bursts; need SRE help to test scale-down behavior.
- Quantization tradeoffs: 4-bit path reduces memory but increased compile time; unclear if net cost reduction for our traffic pattern.
- Measurement: we currently lack token-level attribution for cost across multi-tenant routes (ask data infra).

Confidence check (self):
- KR1: 40% (solid local perf but staging gaps)
- KR2: 30% (need production telemetry to validate)
- KR3: 60% (rollout infra in place, risk on edge cases)

Retrospective notes (what to keep / change):
- Keep: fast iteration with small experiments; bench harness + tracing has been effective.
- Change: instrument earlier in PR cycle — add a quick cost/latency smoke to all model onboarding PRs.
- Personal: over-scheduling pairing sessions blocked deep debugging time; carve 8h/week deep focus.

Next week actions (top 3):
1) Pair with SRE (Asha) to run scale-down test with caching_enabled flag in staging. (Owner: me / Asha)
2) Add quick token-attribution event to the tracing pipeline (reach out to data-infra, open INF-2401).
3) Iterate on kernel swap: address compile-time regression and run multi-region smoke tests (owner: Maya / me).

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Draft a short playbook for fallback behavior when a quantized model exhibits >5% regression on quality.
- Follow up on INF-2345 (batching config edge-case) and update this doc with outcomes.
- Timebox deep debug: block Tue/Thu mornings for investigation.

Random ideas (brain dump):
- Can we expose a "debug-cost" header to surface per-call token cost in the dashboard for 1% of traffic? quick A/B.
- Small experiment: route 2% of requests to a warmed cache layer in a single region to observe tail improvements.

Meeting notes (3/9 check-in with Maya):
- Alignment: prioritise cache + kernel swap; defer multi-model quant experiments until baseline telemetry exists.
- Action: Maya to sync with product for traffic segmentation for safe canaries.

End-of-week quick scorecard (self):
- Progress: ++ (moving pieces in place, measurable improvements in harness)
- Bandwidth: - (context switching)
- Mood: Neutral-positive

Appendix / links to artifacts:
- bench-run-0310.csv (in personal drive folder)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/1024
- Ticket: INF-2345 (batching edge case)

If I forget: next Friday copy this into the weekly OKR summary and mark KRs with traffic-sourced evidence or "needs prod validation" flag.
